title: Local Manager server-managed capability installer boundary

phases.objective: Keep Local Manager capability installer authority server-managed, fail closed before caller-selected grants can be serialized, and use the canonical bounded installer-link TTL without widening Production authority.

e2e_journeys.actor: MAD4B Local Manager signed installer coordinator
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: A capability installer request is prepared for a linked connector device.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Caller-selected capabilities, apps, paths, or shell aliases fail closed before installer-link execution; an empty reconciliation request contains no capability grants and uses the canonical 10-minute TTL. The changed executable is published under distinct version 0.2.27 so SemVer update detection cannot mistake it for the older 0.2.26 build.
steps: Inspect caller-selected capability and permission-grant collections before RequestAsync.
Throw the typed server-managed policy exception when any caller-selected authority is present.
For an empty reconciliation request, serialize only the bounded installer-link fields and omit capability and permission_grants payloads.
Preserve the existing exact non-zero installer exit-code path for genuine repair execution failures.
Bind the changed Windows executable and public fallback URLs to release identity 0.2.27.
assertions: Local Manager cannot submit caller-selected capability authority through the installer link.
The fail-closed error identifies the server-managed policy boundary without exposing credentials.
Capability and permission_grants fields are absent from the installer-link payload.
The requested installer-link TTL is 10 minutes.
No Production deployment, provider mutation, migration, grant, DNS change, secret rotation, or credential creation is performed.
The project, public release fallback, and release-owner route tests agree on version 0.2.27 and never republish the changed executable as 0.2.26.
